ON THE PRECISION OF MCAS SGPS

Update on results presented to April 2013 TAC

BACKGROUND

• October 2012: Derived and reported precision results from simulations based
 upon resampling at the state level.

• Fall 2012: State to transition to anchored SGP analyses (i.e., baseline referenced)
 from previous cohort based analyses.

• April 2013: Derived and reported precision results based upon resampling at
 the individual level for both cohort and anchored analyses.

• October 2013: Update of 2013 MCAS results based upon methodology
 discussed April 2013

METHOD
• Precision estimates for individual SGPs are derived from resampling of SGPs
 using CSEMs from MCAS assessment.

• Student scores (current and rst prior) are simulated using CSEM and SGPs are
 re-calculated based upon perturbed scores.

• Source code for the simulation algorithm is available on GitHub at: https://
 github.com/CenterForAssessment/SGP/blob/master/R/csemScoreSimulator.R
 and CSEMs are available in the embedded SGPstateData meta-data object.

• 100 simulated SGPs are calculated for each student. Standard deviation of the
 simulated SGPs is used as the standard error associated with the individual SGP.

• Simulated SGPs are calculated for both cohort and anchored SGPs. Anchored
 SGPs utilize CSEMs averaged across multiple years.

RESULTS

• The standard error associated with individual SGPs is
 approximately 6 for each grande and content area.

• The maximum standard error associated with individual SGPs
 is 8.85.

• In general, there is greater precision associated with extremely
 low/high SGPs.
